paras: The killing of Bill Holmes was the fatal shooting of a Black man by John Langan at Langan's grocery store in Louisville, Kentucky, reported in a dispatch dated August 5, 1880. The only report found, a one-sentence wire item, said Holmes fired at Langan first after being told to leave, and that Langan then shot him dead.

According to the dispatch, Langan ordered Holmes, whom it called "colored," to go away from his grocery store. Holmes then "pulled a revolver and fired at Langan," the item said, and Langan "whipped out his own revolver and shot the negro dead." The report does not say what led to the order, whether Langan was hurt, who witnessed the exchange, or Langan's race.
No report of an arrest, coroner's inquest, or charge against Langan appears in the coverage found.

The shooting reached print as a single sentence in the Omaha Daily Bee's "Electric Briefs" column, a run of telegraphic items that placed it between Indianapolis campaign news and a Melbourne cabinet notice. The item carried no headline of its own, referred to Holmes as "colored" and "the negro," and gave only the version in which he fired first, without naming its source. No Black-press account, Louisville paper, or follow-up report on the killing was found.

bases: A single named man, John Langan, shot and killed Bill Holmes in a dispute at Langan's grocery; no mob, band, posse or officers are reported (A1).
The only report found is one wire brief in the Omaha Daily Bee (A1); no second paper, local account, or Black-press item was found.

accounts.label: Wire report
accounts.gist: Langan ordered Holmes away from his grocery; Holmes pulled a revolver and fired at Langan, who drew his own revolver and shot Holmes dead. The item does not say who supplied this version, and no other account appears.

framing.detail: The Omaha Daily Bee printed the killing as one telegraphic sentence in its 'Electric Briefs' column, calling Holmes 'colored' and 'the negro' and presenting the shooting as a response to his fire.
